chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah who said, 'I asked Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, 'When does the absentee divorce?' He said, 'Is-haq ibn 'Ammar narrated to me, or Is-haq ibn 'Ammar reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)'
He said, 'When a month passes for him.'
ai.seo_question: When does a husband's divorce take effect if he is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific timeframe for the validity of a divorce pronounced by an absent husband (gha'ib), establishing that the ruling takes effect after the passage of one month. It highlights the jurisprudential consensus among the Imams (peace be upon them) regarding the temporal conditions for marital dissolution when the husband is not present to revoke the divorce immediately, providing a clear legal benchmark for Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Razeyn, form Ibn Sama’at who said, 
‘I asked Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, ‘When can the absentee divorce?’ He said, ‘Is’haq Bin ammar narrated to me, or Is’haq Bin Ammar reported from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or Abu Al-Hasan<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘When a month passes by for him’.
en.sarwar: 8. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah who has said the following: “I once asked Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah about when a man absent from his wife can divorce. He said that Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar narrated to him from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, or abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who said that he can do so after one month.”
